chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Umayr, from Muawiya, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'They say regarding the Hajj of the Mutamatti' that his Hajj is Makki and his Umrah is Iraqi.' He said, 'They are lying. Is it not so that it is linked? He does not exit from it until he fulfills his Hajj.'

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: Hajj of the Mutamatti' (one who combines Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.حَجُّهُ مَكِّيَّةٌ: His Hajj is Makki (performed in Mecca)
key_terms.عُمْرَتُهُ عِرَاقِيَّةٌ: His Umrah is Iraqi (performed in Iraq/Mina area)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on whether the Umrah and Hajj of a Mutamatti' are separate or linked?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the view that the Umrah and Hajj of a Mutamatti' are distinct, independent rituals by emphasizing their juridical unity; the pilgrim remains bound to the state of Hajj until its obligations are fulfilled. This highlights the Shia principle that the Umrah al-Mufradah performed in Dhu al-Hijjah is intrinsically linked to the subsequent Hajj, rather than being a separate, geographically distinct act. The hadith underscores the continuity of the pilgrim's ritual state, ensuring that the transition from Umrah to Hajj is seamless and legally coherent.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Umeyr, from Muawiya who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘They (people) are saying regarding the Tamatto Hajj, is a Makkan Hajj, and its Umra is Iraqi’. So heasws said: ‘They are lying! Or is it not so that it is linked? He cannot come out from it until he fulfils his Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 16. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One who does not have the offering animal with him and he performs Mufrid al-Hajj to keep away from al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous), he has kept away from the religion of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
